canonical.:question/problem:
Find the exact value of $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{12}\right)$ without using a calculator.

*Hint: Use the fact that $$
\displaystyle \dfrac{\pi}{12} = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}.
$$*
canonical.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\sin(x-y) = \sin x\cos y - \cos x\sin y
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $y = \dfrac{\pi}{4},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{12}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\right)\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{4}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{3}\right)\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{4}\right) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{5\pi }{12}\right)?$

*Hint: Use the fact that $$
\displaystyle \frac{5\pi }{12}=\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{6}.
$$*
imports.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $y=\frac{\pi }{6}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{5\pi }{12}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{6}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{4}\right)\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{6}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{4}\right)\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{6}\right) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

imports.:question/problem: What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡({75}^{∘})?$
imports.:question/worked-solution:
The angle ${75}^{∘}$ is not a special angle. However, we can rewrite it as the sum of two special angles, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{75}^{∘}={45}^{∘}+{30}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We now recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $x={45}^{∘}$ and $y={30}^{∘},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡({75}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({45}^{∘}+{30}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

imports.:question/problem:
Using the fact that ${75}^{∘}={135}^{∘}-{60}^{∘},$
calculate the **exact** value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡{75}^{∘}.$

$\operatorname{sin}⁡({75}^{∘})=$
{{field-1}}
imports.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $x={135}^{∘}$ and $y={60}^{∘},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡{75}^{∘} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({135}^{∘}-{60}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{135}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{60}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡{135}^{∘}\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}-\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}+\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

imports.:question/problem:
What is the exact value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(-{105}^{∘})?$

*Hint: Use the fact that $-{105}^{∘}={30}^{∘}-{135}^{∘}.$*
imports.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $x={30}^{∘}$ and $y={135}^{∘},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-{105}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡({30}^{∘}-{135}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{135}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}\operatorname{sin}⁡{135}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

imports.:question/problem:

*Hint: Use the fact that $$
\displaystyle \frac{11\pi }{12}=\frac{7\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{4}.
$$*
imports.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡y
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $x=\frac{7\pi }{6}$ and $y=\frac{\pi }{4}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{11\pi }{12}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{7\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{4}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{7\pi }{6}\right)\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{4}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{7\pi }{6}\right)\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{4}\right) \\  & =\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
